title: Conflict and rivalry
theme: Arguments, grudges, competition over a stall spot or a job, and the confrontation that never comes.

storylets.title: Whose corner is this
storylets.note: Two stall workers argue over a pitch. Chain: cnf.pitch-truce or a cold war.

b1: {A} drags a folding table to the corner and unfolds it with a bang.
{A} hauls crates to a spot by the pond and starts stacking.
{A} carries an awning pole to the corner and sets it down.
b2: {B.desc} strides up and plants both hands on the table. They argue over the paint line on the stone.
{A} and {B.desc} shout across the table, pointing at the same square of sidewalk.
{B.desc} snaps at {A}. {A} snaps back and holds the table down.
b3: {B.desc} leaves, kicking a crate.
{B.desc} turns and walks off, muttering at the sky.
{B.desc} stalks away to the far end of the square.

log: Overheard: {A} shouts: "Fifteen years I have had this corner! You are the new one here!"
Overheard: {B.desc} shouts: "The permit says whoever is first. I was first."

storylets.title: A chalk line down the middle

b1: {A} and {B.desc} stand either side of a chalk mark on the stone.
{B.desc} and {A} face each other across a fresh chalk line.
{A} stands by the pond. {B.desc} stands a pace away with a stick of chalk.
b2: {A} points at the line and then at {A.his} table. {B.desc} shrugs.
{A} gestures toward the left half. {B.desc} nods grudgingly.
{A} indicates the new border and waits.
b3: {B.desc} hands {A} the chalk. {A} adds a mark and passes it back.
{B.desc} holds out a hand. {A} shakes it, quick.
{B.desc} passes over a sweet bun, stiff as a flag.

storylets.title: Someone steps in front
storylets.note: A queue squabble. Small, common, and over in a minute.

b1: {A} waits in line at the counter, a handset in one hand.
{A} stands third in the stall queue, reading the menu.
{A} queues at the stall, shifting from foot to foot.
b2: {B.desc} slides into line ahead of {A}, shoulder first.
{B.desc} steps in front of {A} and orders without looking back.
{B.desc} cuts the queue and nudges {A} aside.
b3: {A} says something sharp. {B.desc} shrugs it off. {A} shakes {A.his} head.
{A} shrugs and lets it go, mouthing a word.
{A} turns away from {B.desc}, jaw working.

storylets.title: Two coworkers, one door
storylets.note: A work rivalry. Observation of body language and a few overheard words.

B.desc: a coworker, a rival for the same post

b1: {A} stands at the work door, badge held in one fist.
{A} waits outside the workplace with arms crossed and a jaw set.
{A} lingers at the door, shifting a bag from shoulder to shoulder.
b2: {B.desc} comes up. A few words, clipped. Neither smiles.
{B.desc} says something short to {A}. {A} answers with a flat sentence.
{A} and {B.desc} speak at the door without looking at each other.
b3: {B.desc} goes in first and lets the door slide shut on {A}.
{B.desc} enters and does not hold the door.
{B.desc} steps through the door and it closes behind.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "Congratulations on the posting. Hope the extra hours are worth it."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "It was a fair vote. Take it up with the floor manager."

storylets.title: A look held a beat too long
storylets.note: Two people with a history cross paths. Observed only.

B.desc: someone A has a grudge with

b1: {A} cuts across the square, hands in pockets.
{A} walks the south side at a steady pace.
{A} heads for the stalls with eyes on the ground.
b2: {B.desc} stands by the pond with arms folded and watches {A} cross.
{B.desc} stays still at the rail, turning to follow {A}.
{B.desc} idles at the fountain edge with a hard stare.
b3: {A} passes {B.desc} at arm's length and does not break stride.
{A} goes by {B.desc} without a word, jaw tight.
{A} steps wide around {B.desc} and keeps going.

storylets.title: The confrontation that does not happen
storylets.note: A walks at someone with purpose, stops, and goes away again. Never resolved; that is the point.

b1: {A} strides across the square toward the stalls, one fist clenched.
{A} marches at the cafe stools with a face like a shut door.
{A} heads for the counter, quick and purposeful.
b2: {A} stops two paces short of a seated figure and stays there.
{A} halts and stands with a hand half raised.
{A} stays rooted a step from the stool, mouth working.
b3: {A} shakes {A.his} head, turns away, and goes back the way {A.he} came.
{A} drops the hand, shrugs, and turns away.
{A} turns on a heel and leaves, the fist opening slowly.

storylets.title: A word about the thirty
storylets.note: A creditor catches someone at a stall. Chain: cnf.debt-settled or never paid.

b1: {A} stands at a stall counter and counts coins into a palm.
{A} queues for a bowl, thumbing a short stack of notes.
{A} reaches the counter and pats a pocket twice.
b2: {B.desc} steps up behind {A} and speaks low. {A} stiffens.
{B.desc} taps {A} on the arm and says a few words. {A} turns slowly.
{A} and {B.desc} talk, {B.desc} calm, {A} not.
b3: {A} hands over a few notes. {B.desc} counts them and frowns.
{A} holds out a small fold of cash. {B.desc} takes it without a word.
{A} passes {B.desc} what is in the pocket and nothing more.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "That is all I have until the fifteenth. Not a note more."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "You said that last month. Twice."

storylets.title: The rest of it, in an envelope

b1: {B.desc} stands at the counter, tablet under one arm.
{B.desc} waits at the stall edge with a flat expression.
{B.desc} leans on the rail by the stalls.
b2: {A} comes up and hands over a thick envelope. {B.desc} counts it, then counts it again.
{A} holds out the envelope with both hands. {B.desc} takes it.
{A} passes the envelope across and says four words.
b3: {B.desc} nods once and leaves without a word.
{B.desc} tucks the envelope away and walks off.
{B.desc} goes, tapping the tablet.

storylets.title: Posted at a rival
storylets.note: A vague feed post that reads like a dig. The monitor reports the post, not who it is about.

b1: {A} sits on a bench with jaw set and a thumb moving fast.
{A} takes a seat and types with both thumbs, hard.
{A} perches on the bench edge, scrolling with a scowl.
b2: {A} posts and puts the handset face down on the slats.
{A} posts, deletes, posts again.
{A} sends a post and shoves the handset into a pocket.

log: Posted: "Some people copy your recipe and call it theirs. You know who you are."
Posted: "Funny how the best spots go to whoever shouts loudest."
